title: The Female Eunuch
author: Germaine Greer
target_audience: Adults interested in gender issues and feminist theory
Scholars and students of sociology, literature, and women's studies
Readers seeking to understand women's liberation movements
Anyone interested in the history of social change and gender roles
core_themes: Critique of traditional family and gender roles
Reclamation of female identity and agency
primary_purpose: To challenge prevailing social norms and inspire women to recognize and break free from the constraints of patriarchy, advocating for sexual and personal liberation as essential to true equality.

structure_format.organization: Divided into thematic sections: Body, Soul, Love, and Hate, each dissecting different aspects of women's experience under patriarchy

key_concepts_lessons: Women are culturally castrated—'eunuchs'—by traditional expectations and roles.
Sexual repression is central to the broader oppression of women.
Conventional family structures and consumer society reinforce gender inequality.
True liberation requires women to reclaim their bodies, desires, and voices.
Patriarchal systems persist through both overt and internalized mechanisms.
notable_features: Combines scholarship, polemic, and personal insight
Sparks debate and criticism even decades after publication
cultural_historical_context: Published at the height of the second-wave feminist movement, 'The Female Eunuch' became emblematic of the era’s call for fundamental social change, challenging post-war Western gender roles and sparking international debate about sex, power, and womanhood.
reception_impact: Lauded as a catalyst for debate and consciousness-raising
Helped shape feminist discourse in the 1970s and beyond
Criticized for lack of intersectionality and focus on white, Western women
Remains influential in feminist theory and literature
comparable_titles: The Second Sex by Simone de Beauvoir
The Feminine Mystique by Betty Friedan
